subject: veterinary-medicine
intro: Veterinary medicine leads to the people who keep animals well and food safe — clinicians at the bench and the farm gate, herd-health planners and the public-health vets who watch the animal–human disease border.

roles.title: Veterinarians
roles.what: Protect animal health and welfare: diagnose and treat sick and injured animals, vaccinate and medicate, perform surgery, and advise owners on care. Some vets also inspect livestock and test for transmissible diseases that threaten people.
roles.where: Every species unit maps onto the job — companion animal medicine and surgery, equine colic and lameness, food-animal herd health — while unit 7's zoonoses and One Health topics are the public-health half of the licence.

roles.title: Veterinary Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Do the clinical work around the vet: take histories and vital signs, collect and run laboratory samples, take radiographs, bandage wounds, anaesthetise and monitor patients, and give owners home-care instructions.
roles.where: The diagnostics and imaging unit — clinical pathology, radiography and ultrasound, laboratory interpretation — plus the asepsis and anaesthesia topics from the surgery unit are this role's daily toolkit.

roles.title: Veterinary Assistants and Laboratory Animal Caretakers
roles.what: Keep animals and clinics running: feed, bathe and exercise animals, monitor them after surgery, disinfect kennels and equipment, restrain patients safely during exams, and prepare specimens for the laboratory.
roles.where: The restraint and safe-handling content behind preventive care units, the hygiene logic of biosecurity and asepsis, and the client-communication strand of practice management all show up at this first rung of the clinic ladder.

roles.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
roles.what: Study animals and their ecosystems: run field and laboratory research on wildlife populations, track disease and reproduction, estimate population sizes, and advise on conservation and wildlife management plans.
roles.where: The comparative anatomy and physiology unit and the parasitology, herd-immunity and disease-ecology topics from the food-animal and public-health units give the biological grounding field wildlife work assumes.

roles.title: Epidemiologists
roles.what: Investigate patterns of disease and who gets them: trace outbreaks, run surveillance studies, analyse risk factors, and design the prevention and control measures that stop epidemics in animal and human populations.
roles.where: Unit 7 is the direct feeder — zoonoses, meat inspection and food safety, herd immunity and biosecurity, and the One Health framing that links veterinary surveillance to human health protection.
